findings.description: The bucket sets no ACL (and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource exists anywhere in the file), and the inline comment confirms it is intended to be public. It holds a customer master spreadsheet, so anonymous internet users could read sensitive customer records.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so objects such as customer-master.xlsx are stored without enforced SSE-KMS/SSE-S3 encryption.
No logging block is configured, so unauthorised access to this publicly exposed bucket containing customer data would leave no audit trail for detection or forensics.
Object versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, so objects overwritten or deleted maliciously cannot be recovered and the bucket can be emptied and destroyed outright.

No bucket policy denying requests with aws:SecureTransport = false is attached to any bucket in this file, so objects may be read or written over plaintext HTTP. This is most acute for the public bucket.
A customer master spreadsheet (customer-master.xlsx) is uploaded into aws_s3_bucket.data, which is public and unencrypted, directly exposing sensitive customer records to anonymous readers.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for a bucket holding financial data, so objects are stored without enforced encryption at rest.
No logging block is configured, so access to financial data cannot be audited or investigated after a compromise.
Object versioning is not enabled while force_destroy = true, leaving financial objects unrecoverable after malicious overwrite or deletion.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is present, so operations data is stored without enforced server-side encryption.
No logging block is configured for this bucket, removing the audit trail for object-level access.
No server_side_encryption_configuration block is defined, so data science datasets are stored unencrypted at rest even though this bucket is otherwise hardened with versioning and logging.

The log bucket relies solely on the log-delivery-write ACL and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource is defined for it (or any other bucket here), so a later ACL or bucket-policy change could expose audit logs publicly.
